issues.legal_issue: A notification extending boundary-alteration provisions to a notified area under a repealed municipal enactment continues under a reenacted enactment when it is neither expressly superseded nor inconsistent with the new enactment.
material_facts: A notification under the former municipal enactment extended provisions governing the inclusion or exclusion of local areas to a notified area and its town committee.
The former municipal enactment was repealed and replaced by a new municipal enactment.
The new enactment did not expressly supersede the earlier notification, and the notification's continued operation was not inconsistent with the new enactment.
The government later issued notices to include a contiguous part of a tea estate within the town committee area under the new enactment.
issues.conclusion: The earlier notification continued in force and was deemed to have been issued under the new enactment. The government was therefore competent to include a contiguous local area within the town committee area.
issues.legal_principle: Section 26 of the Assam General Clauses Act, 1915 provides that, where an enactment is repealed and reenacted, a notification made under the repealed enactment continues in force and is deemed made under the reenacted enactment unless otherwise expressly provided or inconsistent with the reenacted provisions. Because the notification extended the former Act's area-alteration provisions to the notified area, and the new Act empowered the government to include a contiguous local area, the earlier notification supported action under the new Act. The court relied on no earlier cases for this ruling.

rule.if: challenge_to_boundary_notification and prior_extension_notification and municipal_law_repealed_and_reenacted and no_express_supersession and continuance_not_inconsistent and new_law_authorizes_contiguous_inclusion

predicates.challenge_to_boundary_notification: A party challenged a government notification that altered the boundaries of a town committee area.
predicates.prior_extension_notification: The government had previously issued a notification extending area-alteration provisions to a notified area and its town committee.
predicates.municipal_law_repealed_and_reenacted: The enactment under which the earlier notification was issued was repealed and replaced by a new municipal enactment.
predicates.no_express_supersession: The new enactment contained no express provision superseding the earlier notification.
predicates.continuance_not_inconsistent: The continued operation of the earlier notification was not inconsistent with the provisions of the new enactment.
predicates.new_law_authorizes_contiguous_inclusion: The new enactment empowered the government to include a local area contiguous to the town committee area.

issues.definition: When a boundary-notification challenge concerns an earlier extension notification under a repealed and reenacted municipal law, and the new law neither expressly supersedes that notification nor conflicts with its continuation while authorizing contiguous inclusion, the government may include a contiguous area under the reenacted law.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment that adds notifications to a statutory saving clause does not save notifications issued under a repealed enactment for the period before the amendment came into force when the amendment has no retrospective effect.
material_facts: The municipal enactment was repealed and replaced before the amendment was enacted.
The original saving clause did not expressly list notifications among the saved matters.
A later amendment added notifications to the saving clause and came into force after publication in the official gazette.
The amendment did not receive retrospective operation.
issues.conclusion: The amendment did not retrospectively save the earlier notification; its continued force was instead supported by the general saving rule in the Assam General Clauses Act.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the 1958 amending Act came into force upon publication and was not given retrospective operation. Its addition of notifications to the saving clause therefore could not itself save notifications for the earlier period. The court relied on no earlier cases for this ruling.

rule.if: earlier_notification_under_repealed_law and original_saving_clause_omitted_notifications and later_amendment_added_notifications and amendment_not_retrospective

predicates.earlier_notification_under_repealed_law: The government had issued a notification under an enactment before that enactment was repealed.
predicates.original_saving_clause_omitted_notificat: The original saving clause did not expressly include notifications among the matters preserved on repeal.
predicates.later_amendment_added_notifications: A later amendment added notifications to the saving clause.
predicates.amendment_not_retrospective: The amendment was not given effect for a period before it came into force.

issues.definition: When an earlier notification was issued under a repealed enactment, the original saving clause omitted notifications, and a later amendment added them without retrospective effect, that amendment does not save the earlier notification for the prior period.
